---
title: PubTator3
description: PubTator3's five concept files landed whole, and one derived table of which genes, diseases, chemicals, species and variants each paper mentions.
---

[PubTator3](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/pubtator3/) (Lu lab, NCBI)
tags genes, diseases, chemicals, species and variants in PubMed abstracts and
PMC full text, and merges curated links from gene2pubmed, MeSH, CTD, ClinVar
and others. It publishes one headerless TSV per entity type, regenerated
together about monthly. The release lands the five files whole, one table
each, and derives `annotation.pubtator3__mention`: one row per (paper,
concept, asserting resource). There is no version, so the version is the
retrieval date.

## Licence and citation

Public domain, per the FTP directory's README. Cite PubTator3 as
[its site asks](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/pubtator3/).

## Join keys

- `pmid` joins `annotation.pubmed__article` and the iCite tables.
- `concept_id` is an Entrez GeneID for genes (joins `annotation.ncbi__gene.gene_id`), a MeSH or OMIM id for diseases, MeSH for chemicals, an NCBI Taxonomy id for species, and a tmVar id for mutations; `concept_type` says which.
- `resource` is in the key, one row per asserting resource, so "curated links only" is a filter (`resource <> 'PubTator3'`).

## Good to know

- The mention strings stay in raw: they move with every tagger retrain. Join back on (`pmid`, `concept_id`) to read them.
- Mentions PubTator3 recognised but could not normalise have concept id `-` in raw and are not derived.
- A gene mention that resolves to several ids (`6900;1491938`) becomes one row per id; mutation ids are never split.
